transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I came in because my eating feels out of my control. Once I start, it’s like my hands just keep reaching for more food, even while I’m telling myself, “Tom, stop this right now.” It scares me.
Do you have a fear of gaining weight or feel that your body shape impacts how you see yourself?
Yes. I know my doctor says I’m too thin, but if the scale goes up even half a pound, I get panicky. I feel ashamed, like I’ve let myself go and I need to fix it right away.
After eating, do you ever make yourself sick or use laxatives to try to control your weight?

Yes… I do. If I feel like I ate too much, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw it back up. And I’ve taken laxatives too, because I get scared the food is going to stay in me and make me gain weight.
Do you usually make yourself sick or use laxatives only after eating a large amount of food, or do you sometimes do this even after eating a small or normal-sized meal?
Usually it’s after I feel like I ate too much. Then I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself bring it up. I’ve used laxatives too, because I get scared the food is just going to stay in me.
Do you find yourself eating a large amount of food in one sitting, even when you’re not hungry, and feel like you can’t stop once you start?

Yes. That’s the part that scares me most. Once I start eating, it feels like my hands just keep reaching for more, even while I’m telling myself, “Tom, stop this right now.” It’s like I can’t make myself stop in the moment.
When you're eating a large amount of food in one sitting, do you feel like you’ve completely lost control over your eating, like you can’t stop or regulate what you’re doing?
Yes. It really does feel like I’ve lost control. I’ll be telling myself, Tom, stop, that’s enough, but my hands just keep going back for more. That’s the part that scares me.
How often do these episodes of eating a lot and then making yourself sick happen? Would you say they occur at least once a week?

Yes… at least once a week. I’ve been keeping food logs, and looking back, for many months now there’s been nearly every week where I had an afternoon that got out of control, and then I tried to make up for it somehow—throwing up, laxatives, not eating after, or pushing myself with walking and chores.

Do these episodes of eating and trying to compensate for it ever interfere with your daily life—like making it hard to focus on work, causing you to avoid social situations, or affecting your relationships?

Yes, it has. I’ve stopped going to my garden group much, and I avoid family meals more than I used to. I’m either trying to plan around the food, or I feel ashamed afterward, or I’m worried someone will notice what I’m doing. It’s made me pull back from people.
